lines.li: [us] Who decides things among your people?
[them,town:head] The elders talk until the fire burns down, and then {HEAD} says what they decided.
[them] The elders talk until the fire burns down, and then someone says it aloud.
[us] That sounds slow.
[them] Slow fires burn longest, we say.
[us] I'll remember that one.
[us] Do you hunt, back home?
[them,them:best:Shooting|them:best:Melee] I bring meat home more often than most, and I don't boast of it.
[them] Everyone hunts, even those who are bad at it, and I am not the worst.
[us] What do you hunt?
[them,home:desert] Whatever the sand lets live, which isn't much.
[them,home:frozen] Whatever stands still long enough in the snow.
[them,home:jungle|home:swamp] Whatever doesn't bite us first.
[them] Whatever the season brings close to camp.
[us] And you thank it, I suppose.
[them] Always, or the next one will not come.
[them] How many moons have your people lived on this land?
[us,colony:young] Not many, we're still new here.
[us,colony:old] Enough that we've stopped counting.
[us,!colony:young,!colony:old] A few, enough to know where the water is.
[them] Then the land has started to learn your names.
[them] Have the spirits of this place spoken to you yet?
[us,tribal] Now and then, in the wind before a storm.
[us] Not that I've heard, but I'm not sure I'd know how to listen.
[them] Sit still at dusk, say nothing, and you will hear them.
[them] Among my people a gift is a bond, so be careful who you give to.
[us] Then I'm glad I gave it to you.
[them] So am I, friend.
[them] You build as if you mean to stay forever.
[us] We'd like to.
[them] My people build with hide and wood, so the land can take it back when we go.
[us] Ours would take the land a good while.
[them] So many strange things in one place, I don't know where to look first.
[us] Ask about anything you like.
[them] Then start with whatever it is that hums.
[us] How are children raised among your people?
[them] By everyone, so no child has only one mother to scold them.
[us] That sounds like a lot of scolding.
[them] It is, and a lot of carrying, and a lot of songs.
[them] At home the old ones would be telling stories by now.
[us] Tell me one, then.
[them] Do you know the one about the man who caught the moon in a bucket?
[us] I don't think I do.
[them] He caught it every night, and every morning it had leaked away.
[us] I think I like your stories.
[us] Do names mean something among your people?
[them] Every name is a story, and the elders give it when they know you.
[us] What's the story of yours, then?
[them] I'll tell you when I know you better, that's how it works.
[them] You shared your table with me, so now I owe you a place at my fire.
[us] There's no need.
[them] There is every need, or what kind of guest would I be?
[us] Is the tithe heavy where you come from?
[them] Heavy enough, and the reeve counts every egg twice.
[us] Do you get anything back for it?
[them] A road that's mostly mended and a lord who mostly leaves us be.
[us] Mostly is something.
[them] Aye, mostly is what we live on.
[us] Did you learn your trade from a master?
[them] Seven years an apprentice, and my master still says I do it wrong.
[us] Do you?
[them] Not anymore, but don't tell my master.
[us] Do you ever see {LEADER}, your {LEADERTITLE}?
[them] Only on feast days, riding past with banners, and I bow low enough to see my boots.
[us] Does {LEADER} notice?
[them] The horse does, I think.
[them] A good ale and a warm hearth, that's all a body needs.
[us] And a roof that doesn't leak.
[them] Aye, I'll give you the roof.
[us] Can anyone set up a stall in {TOWN}?
[them] Anyone who pays the guild, swears the oath and keeps honest weights.
[us] And if they don't?
[them] Then they sell from a cart outside the walls, with the tinkers.
[them] My mother would have said a prayer for the road in weather like this.
[us] Would it have helped?
[them] It never hurt, and she always got home.
[us] Is the plowing done where you live?
[them] The oxen are at it from dawn to dusk, and so is everyone behind them.
[us] And they let you go?
[them,role:trader] Somebody has to sell what we grew last year.
[them] I said I'd bring back salt, which bought me a week.
[us] What's a day's work worth in {TOWN} these days?
[them] Less than it was, and more than they want to pay.
[us] Same everywhere, I'd guess.
[them] Same everywhere, and nobody's guessing.
[us] Do you travel with the caravans often?
[them,role:trader] Half the year, and the other half I spend wishing I was.
[them] When they'll have me, it's safer than walking alone.
[us] Safer, but slower.
[them] Slow and alive beats quick and robbed.
[them] We get the news over the radio in {TOWN}, when the weather lets us.
[us,lowtech] We get ours from whoever walks through the gate.
[us] Ours mostly comes from whoever walks up the road.
[them] Then I'd better make mine worth the walk.
[them] Where I'm from, everybody sleeps with a rifle in reach, even the preacher.
[us,lowtech] We keep a blade by the door ourselves, so we're not so different.
[us] We're not so different here, I suppose.
[them] Nobody out here is, once the sun goes down.
[us] Have you always done the work you do?
[them] I've done most work going at one time or another, out here you take what comes.
[us] What was the worst?
[them] Anything with a shovel in midsummer, and I'll say no more about it.
[us] And the best?
[them] Anything that paid on the day.
[them] Settlers, huh, I've seen a lot of you come and go.
[us] We mean to be the ones who stay.
[them] They all say that, but I hope you're right.
[us] Were your people born here, or did they come down from the stars?
[them] Some of each, and nobody agrees which kind is better.
[us] Which are you?
[them] I'd rather not say, it starts arguments.
[us] How long will you stay?
[them] Until our business is done, and I've scheduled it to the hour.
[us] Do you schedule everything?
[them] Everything except the weather, and I've filed a complaint about that.
[them] Somewhere up there, minds bigger than worlds are thinking about things we'll never know.
[us] Does that frighten you?
[them,their:empire] The Empire keeps its eyes on them, so I try not to worry.
[them] Only when I think about it, so I try not to.
[us] You don't say much, do you?
[them] I say exactly as much as I mean, which people take for not much.
[us] I'll take it as exactly enough, then.
[them] Good, we understand each other.
[them] You do all this without power, by hand?
[us] By hand, and with a lot of help from each other.
[them,their:spacer] I've seen whole cities that couldn't manage half of it.
[them] I'm impressed, and I don't say that often.
[us] What do people in {TOWN} argue about?
[them,their:spacer] Data, mostly, and whose numbers are wrong.
[them] Fuel prices, fences and whose turn it is to fix the pump.
[us] It sounds like home.
[them] Every town is the same town with different weather.
[us] Your people and mine haven't always been on speaking terms.
[them] No, and some of mine would rather we still weren't.
[us] And you?
[them,them:kind] I'd rather talk than bleed, and I'm not ashamed of it.
[them] I go where the profit is, and today it's here.
[them] Don't mind my manners, where I'm from you speak plain or not at all.
[us,trait:Abrasive] Plain suits me better than you'd think.
[us] Plain suits me.
[them] Then we'll get on fine.
[them] Nice place, lot of things worth having, if a person were that sort.
[us] And are you that sort?
[them] Not today.
[them] I hear you stood your ground when they came at you.
[us] We did.
[them] Where I'm from, that buys more respect than silver.
[them] My people say yours are soft, and I came to see for myself.
[us] And what do you see?
[them,colony:raid] Soft people don't stand after a raid, so they're wrong.
[them] I haven't decided yet.
[us] Are there rules where you come from?
[them] One rule, don't take what you can't hold.
[us] That's a hard rule.
[them] It's an honest one, which is more than most places can say.
[them] Our peoples stand together now, and I'm glad of it.
[us] So are we.
[them,their:tribal] Then our fires are one fire.
[them,their:empire] Then the Empire has a friend at the edge of things.
[them] Then let's keep it that way.
[us] What do your neighbors call your people?
[them] {PEOPLE}, to our faces, and something ruder when we've gone.
[us] Do your people have a ruder name for us yet?
[them] Give us time.
[them,their:spacer] {OUTSIDER}, of {PEOPLE}, and I'm told you're the people to talk to.
[them] Name's {OUTSIDER}, I'm with {PEOPLE}.
[us] {COLONIST}, and welcome to {COLONY}.
[them] Thanks, it's a long way to anywhere out here.
[us] Do you travel much?
[them,teen] More every year, and I'm not a child, whatever they tell you.
[them,old] I was walking these roads before your colony was a thought.
[them] When I can, there's always more to see.
[us] There is, I'm finding.
